chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu al-Abbas al-Kufi, all of them from Amr ibn Uthman, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The disciples gathered to Jesus (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'O teacher of goodness, guide us.' He said to them, 'Indeed, Moses, the Speaker of God (peace be upon him), ordered you not to swear by God, Blessed and Exalted, while being liars, and I order you not to swear by God, whether liars or truthful.'

They said, 'O Spirit of God, increase it for us.' He said, 'Indeed, Moses, the Prophet of God (peace be upon him), ordered you not to commit adultery, and I order you not to converse with your souls regarding adultery, in addition to actually committing it. Indeed, whoever converses with his soul regarding adultery is like one who lights a fire in a decorated house; the smoke spoils the decorations even if the house does not burn down.'

key_terms.أَنْ تُحَدِّثُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ: To converse with your souls (internal contemplation)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the command of Moses and Jesus regarding swearing and adultery?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia concept of *ziyadat* (incremental spiritual elevation) in the teachings of the Prophets, where Jesus (peace be upon him) refines the legalistic prohibitions of Moses (peace be upon him) into deeper, internal states of being. The metaphor of smoke spoiling a decorated house emphasizes that mere physical avoidance of sin is insufficient if the heart remains occupied by the desire, a key theme in Shia *akhlaq* (ethics) and *tafsir*. It highlights the continuity and perfection of divine guidance, positioning Jesus not as a repeater of Moses' law but as its spiritual expounder.
